---
title: "Building Trishula"
---

Trishula is built and verified with a small, reproducible toolchain. `just` is the entry runner: `just` alone lists every build and lab lane; the procedures stay in the scripts. The kernel-side eBPF sources compile CO-RE on a Linux kernel inside a virtual machine. The userspace Go services follow a test-first engineering standard. Every claim traces to a merge-verified pull request.
This page documents that loop — the same loop that produces the evidence records cited across the [roadmap](roadmap.html).

## The build environment

| Layer | Component | Role |
|---|---|---|
| Entry runner | [`just`](https://github.com/casey/just) | the task registry: `just` lists every lane; one recipe = one delegate to a script |
| Test target | **Linux VM on the workstation** (Ubuntu 24.04, arm64) | The actual eBPF test kernel: verifier, BTF, TC/XDP attach, netns/veth harnesses |
| Kernel toolchain | `clang -target bpf` + `bpftool` | CO-RE compile + `vmlinux.h` generation from the VM kernel's own BTF |
| Object generation | [`bpf2go`](https://github.com/cilium/ebpf) | Generated Go bindings + per-target objects, committed — a tagged release ships byte-identical objects ([the hook inventory](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/blob/main/docs/spec.md#92-hook-inventory)) |
| Loader | [`cilium/ebpf`](https://github.com/cilium/ebpf) | Load/pin/attach from Go; no C loader on the host |

The VM is the test kernel because **eBPF is kernel work**: XDP/TC programs, maps, BTF and the verifier exist only on Linux. The workstation orchestrates; the VM verifies. kind (Kubernetes-in-the-VM) extends the same pattern to the cluster-level labs ([TR-06](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/issues/6)).

## Verification standard

Every build item follows a hypothesis-first test-driven loop (the [engineering standard](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/issues/42), encoded in [CONTRIBUTING](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)):

1. **Spec** — the spec section is the design source; the issue cites its sections ([the spec index](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/issues/56)).
2. **RED** — the failing test is written first and committed watched-failing. A kernel-side contract is frozen by test *before* the C implementation lands. The frozen facts: map names, types, sizes, wire layouts, action codes.
3. **GREEN** — the minimal implementation makes the test pass; nothing more.
4. **PR** — branch per change, GPG-signed commits, CI gates (build + vet + test, dependency review, pre-commit). Every PR carries the hypothesis and the RED/GREEN evidence in the body.
5. **Close on acceptance** — an issue closes only when its own acceptance line is verified against the tree (run the check, paste the evidence).

This produces the property that matters: every roadmap artifact is **proved by a runnable check**, not asserted by prose.

## The kernel-side loop in practice

A real example — the shield PoC ([TR-03](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/issues/65)) and the ring producer ([TR-04](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/issues/4)) — shows the loop end to end:

```text
1. contract test (RED)        map names/types/sizes pinned from [the stage sketches](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/blob/main/docs/spec.md#191-stage-sketches-from-the-code-v0-poc)
2. wire-format test (RED)     ban_key/ban_val byte layouts frozen for C + Go
3. C implementation (GREEN)   bpf/shield_xdp.c + bpf/flow_tc.c compiled
                              -target bpf, verifier-passed
4. loader (GREEN)             cilium/ebpf attach; XDP on the interface,
                              TC clsact on veth pairs
5. E2E (RED → GREEN)          netns + veth + synthetic flow: a banned
                              source drops in-kernel; a real flow
                              decodes with full header fields
6. gate script                lab/verify-xdp-chain.sh — the environment
                              gate every kernel-side PR pastes as evidence
```

Facts the loop surfaced (and the tests now pin): the ring event is 200 bytes (C natural alignment), TCP ports travel network-order, the L7 payload offset follows `tcp->doff`, and payload bytes can sit in paged fragments — linear-only reads never see them, so the peek uses `bpf_skb_load_bytes`. Each was caught by a test during the build and recorded in the PR trail.

## Environment gates

Two gates run before kernel-side work merges:

- **`lab/verify-xdp-chain.sh`** — proves the test host end to end. The proof: BTF present; `vmlinux.h` dumped from the live kernel; a CO-RE probe compiled, verifier-loaded, pinned; XDP attached; clean detach. Exit 0 is pasted into the PR.
- **In-VM E2E tags** — kernel-attach tests run behind build tags (`ingest4d`, `attach`) and are root-gated: CI runs the portable suites; the VM runs the kernel suite.

## What is built, what is needed (the GA view)

The build surface as of 2026-10-25:

- **Built and verified:** the entry surface (`justfile` + `lab/prereq.sh`); the CI gates (the build/vet/test with the CRS rx profile, the cue goldens, the route verifier load, the residue teardown, the fastpath diff); the attestation chain per release (the SLSA provenance + the SPDX SBOM, Rekor-backed); the in-VM E2E families (the ban enforce, the ring, the DoS runner — root-gated build tags).
- **Needed before GA:** the release notes carry the consumer `gh attestation verify` block (the cut recipe requires it); the registry leg for the remote clusters (the lab images on EKS/DOKS = push + pull, #261's follow-up); the NGF 2.x dataplane agent on OrbStack (#259's probe matrix — P1 the process-visibility shim, P2 the agent config surface). The 2026.02/03 trains carry the QUIC/kTLS/DPU lanes. The [upstream drafts](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/issues/97) stay parked — nothing files upstream.

## Engineering records

Work is tracked as issues ([TR-01 …](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/issues)) on the [roadmap board](https://github.com/orgs/trishula-dev/projects/1). Large items are sliced into sub-issues (~1 hour each) with native blocked-by edges. The board shows the dependency order.
Kernel-quirk discoveries are filed as defects ([#80](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/issues/80) — platform fast-path bypasses a TC hook), not absorbed silently. The [spec index](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/issues/56) maps every item to its design sections. The [delivery-gate ledger](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/issues/14#issuecomment-6074999638) tracks the verified capability at each stage.

## The DX1 lab quickstart — one command from clone to the full demo

From [TR-14](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/pull/108) on, the whole exit-gate demo is one command. The prereqs = two layers ([issue #261](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/issues/261)):

1. `just` — the entry runner (brew install just; `just` alone lists the lanes).
2. **docker OR kubernetes** — lab/prereq.sh detects the target and prints what it found: a local kind or OrbStack, a hypervisor VM's node, or a cloud Kubernetes (EKS, DOKS) — point your kubeconfig at it and run.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula && cd trishula
just demo        # ~3 stages, each pass/fail loudly; ends on the hop evidence
```

The direct form (`bash lab/demo.sh`) stays equivalent. The lab needs `go`, `kubectl`, `helm` and one of the two target surfaces. A remote cluster needs its own registry for the lab images (the follow-up leaf on #261); the local targets load the images directly.

The stages it composes (each also = a `just` recipe):

```bash
just setup                    # stage 1 — cluster + NGF + engine + echo (idempotent)
bash lab/dx1/apply-effect.sh  # stage 2 — WAFPolicy apply → operator compile →
                              #           engine hot-reload → 403 on traffic, timed (M9 ≤ 5 s)
bash lab/dx1/verify.sh        # stage 3 — hop evidence (NGF → engine → echo), printed LAST
```

Verify the composition yourself — the demo's stage markers, from the recorded run:

```text
| stage 1 PASS — cluster + NGF + engine + echo up (lab left installed)
| stage 2 PASS — CRD apply → operator compile → engine hot-reload → 403, within budget
| stage 3 PASS — NGF → engine → echo pod hop-by-hop evidenced
== DEMO-OK — lab/demo.sh complete: setup + M9 apply→effect + hop evidence all PASS (lab left running, no teardown)
```

The stage-3 hop transcript (`X-Trishula-Hop: engine`, echo pod body, engine-local `/healthz`) is the demo's closing evidence — recorded verbatim in the repo [README "Proof" section](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula#readme) and on [#6](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/issues/6#issuecomment-6091479891).

## Reproduce it locally

```bash
git clone https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula && cd trishula
just build && just vet                   # the portable lanes
just test                                # the full suite (the CI shape)
go build ./... && go test ./...          # the direct form (any OS)
# kernel suites need Linux (root):
sudo go test -tags attach -run TestBanDropE2E ./internal/shield/ -v
sudo go test -tags ingest4d -run TestFlowTCRingE2E ./internal/engine/ingest/ -v
```

Any Linux host with BTF (`/sys/kernel/btf/vmlinux`) and root works; the gate script above checks the details.
